ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, two objects of the same mass are at the same height, A slides down along a smooth inclined plane fixed on the ground, and B falls freely, finally reaching the same horizontal plane. What is the relationship between the work done by gravity on these two objects?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: The work done by gravity on the two objects is the same
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is an inclined plane fixed on the ground; object A is located near the upper end of the inclined plane and will slide down along the inclined plane; object B is in the air on the left side, at the same height as A's initial position; below is the same horizontal ground, and A reaches the bottom end along the inclined plane, while B reaches this horizontal plane after falling freely. Then reason: The problem states that the two objects have the same mass; let their common vertical height difference from the initial position to the final horizontal plane be h. The work done by gravity depends only on the magnitude of gravity and the vertical height difference, and is independent of the path of motion. For A, although it moves along the inclined plane, it descends vertically by h, so the work done by gravity is W_A=mgh; for B, it falls freely and descends vertically by h, so the work done by gravity is W_B=mgh. Therefore W_A=W_B.
